title: I built an open world crime game with a state sized 50 000km2 procedurally generated map with 4000 towns and cities and fully enterable buildings. Rackets include robberies, loansharking, pimping, drug trafficking and more. Would you be interested in playing it on itch?
author: GKTed
selftext:
In this video, I showcase a few of the simpler mechanics, like pickpocketing crack and drug money from some zoned out homeless people, robbing a few stores, and skipping towns as heat rises, travelling across small cities and towns in an Alpine mountains biome all the way to a big city towards the end of the vid.  
  
Each city has their own distinct districts, businesses, locales, biomes and distinct NPC contacts, and there's a heat system tied to each city that's supposed to either keep your crimes in check, or force you to skip town whenever you go on a crime spree.   
  
I designed the game around being smart about the crimes you do and the heat associated with them, such that every time you die or get max heat, you get busted and lose all money on you and assets you own, thus forcing you to balance whether you wanna build a criminal empire slowly in one town, or go on a crime spree like in this clip and just ditch each city when the cops give you too much attention.

In order to keep the video short, I skipped through rackets like loansharking, pimping and drug dealing, but if anyone's interested I can make separate videos showcasing those rackets as well.

comments.author: Kitchen-Many-8466
comments.body: how many unique interior layouts are you actually generating for those 4000 towns, or is it more like a set of archetypes you're mixing and matching? because if every single building is truly unique procedural interior that's a content problem on its own that's bigger than the map generation

replies.author: GKTed
replies.body:
It's closer to the archetypes approach. The entire build has been developed in just three weeks, so the current pool of interior templates is still relatively small.

The generator uses building-specific layout rules for houses, apartments, shops, offices, warehouses, etc., with procedural variations in dimensions, floor counts, room proportions, mirroring, furnishings and décor. Districts influence which building types appear and some of their styling. You’ll definitely recognize recurring layouts at this stage. Fully enterable describes accessibility, rather than every building having a completely unique floor plan.

I plan to expand the template pool as the other systems become more polished and fleshed out. Right now, the priority is making the gameplay work well: rackets, empire building, NPC interactions, more nuanced economy systems and things to buy, more advanced police and heat as well as the consequences of staying in a city or skipping town. More interior variety is on the roadmap, but at three weeks in, I’m prioritizing what you can actually do in the game and those buildings over endless variations of their floor plans.

replies.author: GKTed
replies.body: Thanks! I absolutely do want to invite the GTA comparisons because the GTA franchise, and GTA 4 in particular is my favorite game of all time. However, what disappoints me most about GTA, and more specifically the direction they seem to be heading in with GTA 6, is that they're all story and millions of scripted events, with GTA 5 and Online having left a pretty bad taste in my mouth in that regard. So this game is a love letter to what I would have wished GTA would have been as a franchise by now: a huge ass country or at least state sized game, with lots of freedom and empire building mechanics. Where instead of holding L2 to hold hands like in GTA 6, here you hold e to inject adrenaline into one of the CI's who's been ratting you to the feds after you've chopped off too many of his limbs with a hacksaw.

There are different districts: those from the clip are industrial, rural, intercity, and the rest I didnt show are: villages, residential, suburban, residential/mixed, working class neighbourhoods, downtowns and uptowns, which are mixed and matched based on the city size and the procedural generation, each with distinct buildings, businesses and things to do. In this clip, I focused on showcasing scale, but if enough people are interested I will post more about the rest of the mechanics.

replies.author: GKTed

There's lots of things to do like loansharking, pimping, drug dealing, organ trafficking, car boosting and an emphasis on emergent mechanics and challenges that occur, that I did not show in this video. I didn't make this build primarily to put it on the market, as a matter of fact I was exploring implementing all mechanics I wish GTA would have had by now, as a hardcore GTA player that 100% all of them from 3 onwards. And I'm already having fun fooling around with it.

replies.author: GKTed
replies.body: I hear you, but here's the thing: haven't you ever had the fantasy of being your own boss in a crime sim game? No stories, no quests, just you and the world, making money in the worst possible humanly imaginable ways. That's the reason I'm calling this game "Scumsters". Sometimes you wanna roleplay being human scum, a monster (while keeping the game away from the AO rating unfortunately) without having to serve 10 lifetimes in prison for it. This game caters precisely to that fantasy without dulling it with story elements and morality, something of which even GTA games can be guilty of in today's corporately safe climate. And for that sensation of ultimate freedom, it needs to have freedom of scale, not just morality. This is for the players who love minecraft but wished they could, for example, chop off an NPC's head and put it in someone's mailbox to send them a message and reduce their influence in the city.

replies.author: GKTed
replies.body:
That's actually a great name, especially because the idea is to make a minecraft and gta cross! I called it Scumsters, but MineCrime (or MeinKrime lol) are also good edgy variants to this name now that you gave me this idea.

But precisely because this emerged as an idea that came from the fact I love both games, I want this to be a game where players make their own stories, whether online or offline. Build in enough emergent systems (just like minecraft has) such that players make their experience with Scumsters their own. For example, maybe I first spawned in a small town with few businesses to rob, but it's full of high attraction prostitutes I can hire that can work the more expensive districts like in uptown. But because I spawned in the small town, there's no uptown/high end districts here, so perhaps the best move is steal a bus or van, load them in the back and take them to the big city, and then load up on crack from the crack dens there to use it to hire more prostitutes from the smaller town regions to take them to the big city.

Or maybe there's a gang there that have lots of dealers on the streets, so I kidnap a dealer, chop his limbs off, buy a cemetery, and put his body in one of the coffins and deliver the coffin to the gang leader's house to send him a message and reduce his influence in one of the districts, where I can now safely plant one of my own dealers.

And so on, there's lots of rackets and mechanics like that I intend to implement in the final build.

replies.author: GKTed
replies.body:
Thanks man, those insights might actually be useful. As a matter of fact, I made this game to specifically cater to the audience that hates the phrase "this might be racist" or "offensive" or whatever. I'm taking the edginess and humor in the direction Rockstar used to have, before they became corporately sanitized. 

As for the slop part, I honestly dgaf what counts as slop as long as I'm enjoying the game I play, whether that's a game made by someone else or me. Way too many devs have forgotten about what is by far the most important part of any game: being fun. And fun in my book is not about having handcrafted haikus or looking at the cool little artstyle in their walking simulator they spent 1000 hours refining by hand. 

Fun to me means tying up an NPC in my basement with a chain and forcing him to make drugs the way Jack Welker forced Jesse Pinkman to do in breaking bad. Or showing an NPC a polaroid pic of one of his dead buddies to pressure him into paying me back, he flips me off, and then I grab him by the throat, take him to the rooftop, and throw him off the building. Or being able to blackmail the chief of police with the picture of that one time he cheated on his wife with my prostitute so he could reduce my heat.

All things you can do in this game btw.

Mechanics wise, I'm implementing everything I fantasized GTA 6 would have had, like in their initial project Americas idea where the game took inspiration from Narcos and you'd be building a drug empire across the US spanning cities like Vice City, Liberty City and Los Santos, before they abandoned it because of development crunch or some such bullshit and instead opted to go the Bonnie and Clyde route which really isn't my cup of tea. 

I'm approaching this project as a gamer first and foremost, and if you played Minecraft, GTA and Manhunt and somehow enjoyed all three, then this is the game for you!

replies.author: GKTed
replies.body: Absolutely, I'm just about to completely overhaul the way the whole wanted system works. Right now, cops are only dangerous if you linger in one place too long at a 3 start wanted level or over (cuz they have shotguns) but I'm going to implement much more aggressive spawn rates, automatic weapons, body armor, swat, feds, snipers, roadblocks and spike strips on higher wanted levels, as well as a search perimeter being instated within a certain radius if you passed a certain wanted level threshold. As for cop contacts with the heat system, there is a contact system where you can pay off or do favors for dirty cops, who may in turn reduce your heat or even turn their attention to your rivals.
